methodology: Predicate reused verbatim from calibre/evaluation/forecast_metrics.py:161-168 over results/m5/full-mscp-wls-struct/forecast-ledger.resolved.parquet: resolved = isfinite(y); scored = resolved AND isfinite(lo_0p9) AND isfinite(hi_0p9); unscored = resolved AND NOT scored (the 21,178,253-row population attributed here). Run is perhorizon (benchmarks/m5/config/full-wls-struct.yaml: conformal.mode=perhorizon, partition=series, calibration_window=10, reconciliation.strategy=wls_struct). by_cause splits the unscored mass by origin geometry, the only signals that vary on this run: warm_up = unscored rows whose per-(unique_id, h) calibrator was not yet ready -- ordering each (unique_id, h) group by forecast_origin, the count of PRIOR resolved origins (y finite, ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING..1 PRECEDING) is < calibration_window (10); residual = the remaining unscored rows with >= 10 prior resolved observations whose bounds are still NaN. residual is an UNDETERMINED cause: the ledger does not persist the calibrator's `ready & isfinite(radii)` decision that nulls the bounds, so the precise reason these >=10-history rows are unscorable is not recoverable from the ledger and is reported honestly rather than split further. warm_up + residual == unscored exactly. Confirmation (reported, not split on): conformal_mode is single-valued for this run (perhorizon over all 60,144,896 rows) and calibration_state_ref / conformal_partition are always populated on unscored rows (unscored_empty_ref_share = 0.0), so the conformal columns do not discriminate the cause -- hence the origin-geometry attribution.
